name: Physical & Energy
oneLiner: The power, cooling, buildings and chip factories that everything else physically runs on.

analogy.text: The land, roads and power lines of a city: invisible until they run out.
analogy.breaks: Roads can be widened in months. Chip factories and grid connections take years and enormous investment, and advanced chip production is concentrated in very few places, so this layer can bottleneck the whole stack at once.

givesAbove: Electricity, cooling and floor space, plus the fabricated chips themselves.
needsBelow: Nothing in the AI stack: it rests on energy markets, land, water and industrial supply chains.

walkthrough.title: An answer starts as electricity
walkthrough.text: Someone asks a chatbot a question. Before any maths happens, the data centre needed a grid connection big enough for a town, which took years to secure.

walkthrough.title: Power in, heat out
walkthrough.text: The electricity flows through substations to racks of AI chips, and nearly all of it turns into heat while the chips work out the answer.

walkthrough.title: Liquid carries the heat away
walkthrough.text: Those racks are so dense that air cannot keep up, so liquid flows through plates on each chip and carries the heat outside.

walkthrough.title: Chips from a handful of factories
walkthrough.text: The chips doing the work came from a few specialised fabs and packaging lines, which is why supply can run short.

walkthrough.title: The bill for one answer
walkthrough.text: Add up the chips, the server, idle machines and cooling, and you get the energy per token. Making that smaller stretches every megawatt the grid can supply.
